question.problem:
Given the vector $u=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$, which of the following vectors are orthogonal to $u?$

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Given the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14124529/assets/fa2e713ddeffb34f10835e87dae31937c15b0a8bfb5d142d1b5c1d11267a972f.svg), which of the following vectors are orthogonal to $\mathbf{u}$?
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14124529/assets/366748868499d47ac76b29348ebdcd4d86b7324e42fa6aa808778c42578f97e5.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
We compute the dot product between $\mathbf{u}$ and each of the listed vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =(-5)\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot (-3)+2\cdot (-4)+0\cdot 9 \\  & =-5+9-8+0 \\  & =-4.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot w & ={u}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {w}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {w}_{4} \\  & =(-5)\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot 2+2\cdot 8+0\cdot 3 \\  & =-10-6+16+0 \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot x & ={u}_{1}\cdot {x}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {x}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {x}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {x}_{4} \\  & =(-5)\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot (-4)+2\cdot (-8)+0\cdot 6 \\  & =-10+12-16+0 \\  & =-14.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the correct answer is $\mathbf{w}$ only.
